QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_18

question.text: Daily standard deviation of Cat III fund returns is 0.80%. Assuming 252 trading days per year, what is the annualised volatility?

explanation.text: The Logic: Daily volatility is converted to annualised volatility using the square-root-of-time rule under an iid-returns assumption: annualised σ = daily σ × √T, where T is the number of trading days per year. With 252 trading days: annualised σ = 0.80% × √252 = 0.80% × 15.874 ≈ 12.70%. This scaling reflects the fact that variance scales linearly with time while standard deviation scales with √time. The Trap: 9.80% uses √150 (wrong day-count). 2.02% uses √6.25 (no real basis). 201.60% multiplies the daily figure by 252 directly, ignoring the square-root scaling and dramatically overstating annualised vol. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (165, 253-256, 321) support standard deviation and volatility concepts in the Cat III/derivatives context but do not give the √252 annualisation rule or the iid-returns framing. The formula above is general quantitative-finance knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
